output.answer: Amazon (AMZN) has split its stock four times, most recently a 20-for-1 split: the board approved it on March 9, 2022, shareholders of record at the close of business on May 27, 2022 received 19 additional shares per share (reflected in accounts around June 3, 2022), and split-adjusted trading began June 6, 2022. It was Amazon's first split in over two decades — before it, the company split 2-for-1 on September 2, 1999, 3-for-1 on January 5, 1999, and 2-for-1 on June 2, 1998. The 2022 announcement also included a $10 billion share-repurchase authorization. No further splits have been announced as of November 2026.
caveats: The exact effective dates and ratios of the three 1998–1999 splits come from a third-party split-history database (StockSplitHistory.com); Amazon's own 1998–1999 press releases were not located, so dates could differ by a day depending on whether an announcement, record, or distribution date is used.
The 2022 split-adjusted trading start (June 6, 2022) was stated as "expected" in the March 2022 8-K; third-party databases and subsequent coverage confirm it was completed as scheduled.
No new split has been announced as of November 2026; a future split decision by Amazon's board could change this.

Amazon's board approved the 20-for-1 split (effected via an amendment to the Restated Certificate of Incorporation, subject to shareholder approval at the May 25, 2022 annual meeting), announced alongside a $10 billion share repurchase authorization.
